parts: What if your A.I. remembered what you told it three months ago?
On Monday, Meta released Muse Wonder, its first frontier A.I. model,
along with a bigger version, called Muse Wonder Full.
The headline feature is what Meta calls active memory:
holding on to what matters to you, over days, weeks and months.
That's the missing piece for A.I. agents.
An assistant that forgets everything is stuck on small tasks.
One that remembers can take on long-running work.
Wonder is open to developers through Meta's paid API.
Wonder Full is limited to subscribers of its coding tool.
The catch: the benchmark scores come from Meta's own testing.
And a model that remembers you raises a bigger question: who controls that memory?
Who owns that memory will decide whether they're trusted.
Three months from now, it might remember.
Make sure you can choose what it keeps.
